name: José L. Pons
title: Professor of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation; Professor of Mechanical Engineering (by courtesy)
department: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation; Mechanical Engineering by courtesy
fitReason: Direct fit for neural time-series models, uncertainty-aware exoskeleton control and human-in-the-loop assistive robotics. Pons leads the distinct Neurorehabilitation and Neural Engineering Laboratory; the university identifies him as the conceptual and supervisory lead of the therapist–exoskeleton research program, not merely an incidental coauthor. Its experimental setting overlaps Hargrove’s entry and should be treated as a shared research collaboration rather than independent evidence from a second facility.

physicalEvidence.summary: The April 2025 primary manuscript verifies bi-LSTM gait-feature estimation and neural command prediction executing on an ExoMotus-X2 with two held-out healthy users on a treadmill and stairs. TensorFlow Lite predictions drive references for a ROS/C++ torque controller. The March 2026 Synthetic Therapist work uses previously collected patient data and live exoskeleton-stream inference, but prospective patient training with that learned therapist remains future work. The separate June 2026 TEPI study physically couples a therapist and patient using virtual spring-damper interactions; its eight-patient evaluation is current physical-program evidence, not itself proof of learned autonomous patient control.

shortVisit.summary: The lab People page offers generic contact to join its team. The dedicated contact page verifies the scientific chair’s public email and AbilityLab location, but neither page specifies external master’s visitors, eight-week projects, remote work or summer 2027 openings.

scoreReasons.fit: 37/40: strong neural control, uncertainty modeling and physical human-robot assistance; specialized rehabilitation rather than general-purpose embodied AI.
scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: actual learned exoskeleton torque assistance directly verified in the 2025 revised primary manuscript; newer clinical data claims carefully delimited.

Pons has a current Northwestern professorship and a concurrent Shirley Ryan AbilityLab appointment. The hospital/university host, employer, sponsor and actual laboratory access must be determined; institutional affiliations alone do not establish the appointment route.

Reuse the existing Northwestern policy review: Visiting Predoctoral Fellow is doctoral-only, while saved Student Intern materials conflict on graduate versus undergraduate eligibility and require school/OISS clarification.

Clinical privileges, participant contact, human-subject protocols and restricted research-data access are separate requirements. A short computational or bench project may avoid some dependencies, but that scope has not been offered.
